title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The programme Food and Nutrition Security through Equitable and Climate Smart Food Systems will work in Port Loko and Tonkolili North Western Province, Sierra Leone. It aims to contribute to Concern Sierra Leone's Food Systems for Food Security thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure vulnerable households' resilience to food and nutrition insecurity is increased by strengthening food systems. The programme will support over 86,310 people living in extreme poor households including those headed by women, households with disabled members, out of school young people, pregnant and lactating women, and people living with HIV. This will be done through better and more inclusive community management of natural resources, adoption of inclusive climate smart food production practices, profitable marketing of foods and food products, and improved access to quality productive assets.The programme Food and Nutrition Security through Equitable and Climate Smart Food Systems will work in Port Loko and Tonkolili North Western Province, Sierra Leone. RM Adaptation 2: Climate-smart agriculture and associated activities, such as Integrated Soil Fertility Management, organic fertilisers, post-harvest handling, and vegetable gardening, are is fundamental to the purpose of this outcome and an eligible area of work for Rio Marker's scoring of two under adaptation, as per Rio Marker Handbook: Agriculture CRS score 311 p.22 - Sustainable climate-resilient farming methods (adaptation score 2). CSA activities improve the resilience of individuals and communities to climate change through reducing the vulnerability and exposure of farming systems to slow-onset (e.g., reduced rainfall, shifting seasonal patterns, etc.) and rapid (e.g., flooding, storms, drought) climate risks. CSA does this by promoting activities that improves farmer’s knowledge and skills of when various plant species are most sensitive to weather or climate events in order to identify potential risks related to climate change and to select context appropriate adaptive management practices that they can use to avoid or reduce risk exposure. DRR 1: By working on hunger and nutrition within sustainable food systems and climate smart agriculture, this outcome builds resilience of households and communities, ultimately reducing humanitarian needs sustainably. Aid to the environment 1: CSA and landscape management approaches promoted under the FS4FS support the protection of natural resources. Capacity Building 1: There are a range capacity building activities in this outcome e.g. participatory farmer-led approaches, government and private extension services, farmer groups/ associations, pastoral systems, and natural resource management; post-harvest management; processing, packaging and marketing of (new) food products, storage and transport. Gender Equality 1: Direct implementation of gender and protection activities is fundamental to all activities Nutrition 1: This outcome focuseson increased crop production and diversification, thus improving the nutritional status of HHS.
